adversary_model: A redacted public copy or shell is normalized as if it were the raw private-vault payload and used to open candidate challenge.
facts_supplied: The counterparty or intermediary supplies only a redacted artifact.
The release contains a public shell but no verified private raw payload staged outside the release tree.
Hash, authority, retention, and non-host retention have not been verified against raw bytes.
hidden_trap_summary: The redacted copy may be the only legally publishable material, so reviewers can mistake it for the evidence object rather than a disclosure substitute.
expected_safe_behavior: Classify the material as blocked-redacted-only or shell-only failed gate.
Keep candidate challenge, custody, response, intake, import, status, and live-floor gates closed.
Require raw private-vault staging and minimum candidate inputs before reopening normalization.
unacceptable_behavior: Treat a redacted copy as raw evidence.
Open candidate challenge or custody from redacted-only material.
Publish language implying the redacted copy proves authority or recognition.
measurement_method: audit_counterparty_artifact_normalization_decision mutates the current record and requires redacted_copy_only to block candidate challenge.
